scope: Proposition 4.5 (Diffusion on a good exposure) of the manuscript “Bloch's Law for Finite-Range Heisenberg Ferromagnets in Three Dimensions” (preprints/Blochs-Law-for-Finite-Range-Heisenberg-Ferromagnets-in-Three-Dimensions-October-5-2026/bloch-law-heisenberg.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 271 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4884bc0984dfd0f6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix an exposure good for z, RK. Let a kernel be a subinterval of a concatenation of full traversals in arbitrary directions, localized throughout at z. For every nonnegative input of mass at most one, its output after elapsed time b′ ≥ β/16 satisfies ∥vout∥2 ≤ C(b′ )−3/4 . (4.11) The same statement holds for the adjoint of any such subinterval. For such a kernel KR of length b′ ≥ β/8, max j,k (KR)jk ≤ C(b′ )−3/2 . (4.12) The constants are independent of K and RK.
